messages.author: 4201c816d32af2ef
messages.subject: using custom CDFs
parts:
Hi.

I'm wanting to use some of the brainarray custom CDFs for exon and
expression arrays. Because the 'chiptype' inside the CEL file header
needs to match the directory names (and I don't know of an easy way to
change the header), I've named the CDF downloaded from brainarray to
match whats in the header.

Ideally, I'd like to process the same data with different CDFs and the
different names of the CDFs would be sufficient to keep the results in
different directories.

Is there any reason why one couldn't override whats in the CEL header
in order to do what I want to do? Or, does that cause other problems?

Mark

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] using custom CDFs
parts:
Hi. Me again.

OK, maybe fitting everything with a custom CDF isn't as
straightforward as I though. BG correction and normalization seems
to work no problem. Fitting the model, you see below that it
estimates for 25102 units, which corresponds to my CDF file
downloaded from brainarray. Below that, it reads something for 54675
cells, which is the number of units/genes in the original CDF file,
which shouldn't have entered into this at all.

(Ahh, I've just discovered that if I call fit(plm,units=NULL), this
error does not get thrown and it *seems* to be fitting everything no
problem).

I tried to track down what findUnitsTodo(.) does but was
unsuccessful. That is where the error happens.

Next up, when calculating residuals, I get a similar error. It
appears that it is reading a cache file to get the number of units
and that is probably the same error as above. Obviously, this
wouldn't be a problem if I didn't run the whole thing with the same
named directory structure. I wasn't able to track down where the
cache file resides, so that I could delete it.

Anyways, after all this chatter, my original question still stands.
Is there a way to process the same data under alternate CDFs? This
is not something I expect to always have to do, but using the
brainarray CDFs definitely is something that we should be able to do.

Thanks!
Mark

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] using custom CDFs
parts: Hi.

On 6/23/07, Mark Robinson <mark.rob...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi.
>
> I'm wanting to use some of the brainarray custom CDFs for exon and
> expression arrays. Because the 'chiptype' inside the CEL file header
> needs to match the directory names (and I don't know of an easy way to
> change the header), I've named the CDF downloaded from brainarray to
> match whats in the header.

Correct. You should never (neither have to) modify your CEL files. I
remember that Karen had the same problem with an Exon data set (see
thread "rma background adjusted cel files Options" March 14, 2007).
See also page "Structure of data set directories". You can turn of
the validation of the chip type, i.e. the assertion that the chip type
according to the CEL header match the chip type according to the CEL
set path. You turn it off by adding argument 'checkChipType=FALSE',
e.g.

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("heart_brain",
chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2", checkChipType=FALSE)

Note, the rule is always that the chip type, and hence the CDF, is
decided from the name of the directory of the CEL files. Thus, for
the above example, you need to have a CDF with pathname:

annotationData/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.CDF

If you want to use a different CDF, say "MyHuEx", then you have to provide

annotationData/chipTypes/MyHuEx/MyHuEx.CDF

and

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("heart_brain", chipType="MyHuEx",
checkChipType=FALSE)

Remember, you can always use file links (Unix or Windows shortcuts) to
link say MyHuEx/MyHuEx.CDF to HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.CDF if the
contents of the two CDF are identical.

You can change the AffymetrixCdfFile object coupled with an
AffymetrixCelSet object by calling setCdf() on the latter.

Hope this helps

/Henrik

PS. The reason for aroma.affymetrix being so strict about path and
file names is so that we there will be *one* standard way of storing
data and annotation files. Any mistakes by the user will then be
detected early on and we will avoid odd and unpredictable side effects
down streams. It will also be much easier to maintain and to document
etc. DS.

> Ideally, I'd like to process the same data with different CDFs and the
> different names of the CDFs would be sufficient to keep the results in
> different directories.
>
> Is there any reason why one couldn't override whats in the CEL header
> in order to do what I want to do? Or, does that cause other problems?
>
> Mark

On 6/24/07, Mark Robinson <mrob...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
>
>
> Alright, I wasn't able to solve this. What I've done is put
> everything in a completely new directory for the custom CDFs, so as
> to not interfere with any of the previous running. I think most of
> my previous problems were caused by the reading of an old cache
> file. Speaking of that, is there a way to clear the cache is
> actually cleared. I called clearCache(.) on numerous objects but
> don't know if it actually did anything.

It sound like your troubleshooting is correct.

I am not sure what your CDFs are? One of them is the
'HG-U133_Plus_2.cdf' provided by Affymetrix and the other a CDF for
the same chip type but with a different layout, correct? If so, this
is a good example of how different the term "chip type" and the term
"CDF" are, although they are often (and incorrectly) used
interchangeably, cf. Bioconductor CDF packages.

The "chip type" uniquely defines the actual chip used (which will
remain the same as soon as it produced in the Affymetrix factory).
The "CDF" the defines now the probes on the chip should grouped so
they match a specific analysis. Most often there is one CDF per chip
type, but in some cases, like yours there may be many different CDFs
per chip type. Contrary, there is one and only one chip type per CDF.

So, the take-home message is that two different CDFs should never have
the same name. To use a different CDF for a data set, look up the new
CDF with cdf2 <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromName() and call setCdf(cs,
cdf2) on the AffymetrixCelSet object 'cs'.

The clearCache() method only clears the in-memory cache, not the file
cache. [I know, this is not easy know and it is not 100% clear when
the file cache is used and when the in-memory cache is used.
Hopefully it will be clearer in the future.]. To clear the file
cache, which seems to be the problem in your case (and which shouldn't
reoccur if you name the CDFs differently), delete the corresponding
cache files. You can find the path to the aroma.affymetrix cache
files with getCachePath("aroma.affymetrix"), e.g.

> list.files(getCachePath("aroma.affymetrix"))
[1] "Mapping250K_Nsp" "Mapping250K_Nsp,monocell"
[3] "Mapping50K_Hind240" "Mapping50K_Hind240,monocell"
[5] "Mapping50K_Xba240" "Mapping50K_Xba240,monocell"

As you see, each CDF has its own subdirectory to make it easy to clear
the cache files for a particular CDF.

>
> I have two separate errors, on 2 different datasets. What I've given
> below may not be enough to diagnose it.

I am not sure what these errors are, but see if my suggestions this
far solves you problem. If not, repost together with the script you
are using.

/Henrik

parts:
OK, my cache problems are over and done with. New problem.

I've simplified my calling of my 'pipeline' of BG correction,
normalization, fitting, residuals into the following:

# simplified
# -----------
library(aroma.affymetrix)
name <- "affy_mix"
chip1<- "Hs133P_Hs_REFSEQ"
e1<-doEverything(name,chip1)
# -----------
doEverything<-function(name,chip,force=F) {
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8); timestampOn(verbose)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chip)
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip,
checkChipType=FALSE)
setCdf(cs, cdf)
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose,force=force)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose,force=force) #time required
plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose,units=NULL) #time required
qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
d<-getExprs(chp)
rs<-calculateResiduals(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
ws<-calculateWeights(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
list(d=d,cs=csN,cdf=cdf,plm=plm,qam=qam,chp=chp,res=rs,wts=ws)
}
# -----------

This just returns a list of references to the objects that may be
needed. Now, it actually runs through the first time with no
problems. Once I exited the session and tried to recreate my list of
references to objects (now that isDone is TRUE), it gave an error that:

getOutputDataSet.Transform<-

function (this, ..., force = FALSE)
{
outputDataSet <- this$.outputDataSet
if (force || is.null(outputDataSet)) {
if (isDone(this)) {
ds <- getInputDataSet(this)
clazz <- Class$forName(class(ds)[1])
outputDataSet <- clazz$fromFiles(path = getPath
(this),...) # MR changed this

setCdf(outputDataSet, getCdf(ds))
this$.outputDataSet <- outputDataSet
}
}
outputDataSet
}

process.RmaBackgroundCorrection<-
function (this, ..., force = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
{
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(verbose)
if (verbose) {
pushState(verbose)
on.exit(popState(verbose))
}
verbose && enter(verbose, "Background correcting data set")
if (!force && isDone(this)) {
verbose && cat(verbose, "Already background corrected")
verbose && exit(verbose)
outputDataSet <- getOutputDataSet(this,...) # MR changed this
return(invisible(outputDataSet))
}
ds <- getInputDataSet(this)
params <- getParameters(this)
outputPath <- getPath(this)
args <- c(list(ds, path = outputPath, verbose = verbose,
overwrite = force), params)
outputDataSet <- do.call("bgAdjustRma", args = args)
gc <- gc()
verbose && print(verbose, gc)
verbose && exit(verbose)
this$.outputDataSet <- outputDataSet
outputDataSet
}


process.QuantileNormalization<-
function (this, ..., force = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
{
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(verbose)
if (verbose) {
pushState(verbose)
on.exit(popState(verbose))
}
verbose && enter(verbose, "Quantile normalizing data set")
if (!force && isDone(this)) {
verbose && cat(verbose, "Already normalized")
verbose && exit(verbose)
outputDataSet <- getOutputDataSet(this,...) # MR changed this
return(invisible(outputDataSet))
}
verbose && enter(verbose, "Retrieving target distribution")
getTargetDistribution(this, verbose = less(verbose))
verbose && exit(verbose)
ds <- getInputDataSet(this)
params <- getParameters(this)
outputPath <- getPath(this)
verbose && enter(verbose, "Normalizing data towards target
distribution")
names(params) <- gsub(".targetDistribution", "xTarget", names
(params))
args <- c(list(ds, path = outputPath, verbose = verbose),
params)
rm(params)
gc()
outputDataSet <- do.call("normalizeQuantile", args = args)
gc <- gc()
verbose && print(verbose, gc)
verbose && exit(verbose)
this$outputDataSet <- outputDataSet
verbose && exit(verbose)
outputDataSet
}

Hi Mark,

it looks like you're start understanding the design of
aroma.affymetrix. I have been thinking a little bit more about your
problem/suggestion and think it is safe to assume that a Transform
class generates a valid output data set, that is, we can turn of the
validation of the chip type in getOutputSet(). That would leave you
with a simple modification:

getOutputDataSet.Transform<- function (this, ..., force=FALSE) {
outputDataSet <- this$.outputDataSet;
if (force || is.null(outputDataSet)) {
if (isDone(this)) {
ds <- getInputDataSet(this);
clazz <- Class$forName(class(ds)[1]);
outputDataSet <- clazz$fromFiles(path=getPath(this),
checkChipType=FALSE, ...) ; # MR/HB changed this

setCdf(outputDataSet, getCdf(ds));
this$.outputDataSet <- outputDataSet;
}
}

outputDataSet;
}

I believe that is enough. I've went the code and looked for
potentially problematic fromFiles() calls, but I think the above is
pretty much the only one. However, to be on the safe side, I've added
'...' where applicable. I've added a simple redundancy test using the
above and it seems to work, but could you also see if it works with
you scripts. Then I can commit an updated version of the package.

Cheers

Henrik
